results.outcome: male-higher pair differences in work RVU
results.range_type: Across selected code pairs, not a confidence interval

studies.uncertainty: Methods say mean differences and 95% confidence intervals were used; numerical intervals, exact P values and precision are absent from the accessed abstract. A null test is not proof of equivalence.

source_discrepancy.companion_table: 19 unique CPT rows; female lesion code 56501 is displayed between two male lesion codes 54057 and 54050
source_discrepancy.handling: Use journal counts as the primary report; flag discrepancy and seek peer-reviewed full text. Do not treat the companion as another study or infer a definitive explanation.

reviewer_concerns_not_formal_risk_of_bia: Strict comparator selection improves work comparability but restricts inference to this small code set.
Selection by specialty representatives and procedural exclusions need transparent full-text appraisal; this does not establish biased conduct.
No numerical intervals are available to assess whether clinically important differences remain compatible with the data.
The authors' criticism of earlier comparisons is interpretation, not an independent adjudication of those studies.
studies.proposed_status: Retain explicitly as null/opposing evidence; full-text uncertainty, valuation year and pair-count discrepancy pending.

studies.title: Reimbursement for Female-Specific Compared With Male-Specific Procedures Over Time
studies.access_level: Full author manuscript including Methods, Results, Discussion and Table 1 retrieved through public NCBI PMC EFetch XML. Free full text; Europe PMC does not mark an open-access license.

payer_year.operative_time_data: ACS NSQIP 2015-2018; not a Medicare-only claims cohort; payer and entitlement strata not reported
payer_year.compensation_rates: SullivanCotter 2018 specialty median dollars/RVU versus McGraw-Hill 1994 specialty compensation; not Medicare fee-schedule conversion factors

studies.unit: Procedure codes with observed registry operative times; modeled specialty compensation

comparator.construction: 12 of 24 pairs in earlier research, selected for anatomic/technical similarity and availability in NSQIP; minor procedures absent. Simple and complex scrotoplasty pooled against perineoplasty.
comparator.exclusion: Cases with other or concurrent CPT codes excluded
comparator.time_measure: Observed median intraoperative time per CPT; perioperative and anesthesia time excluded
comparator.normalization: RVU divided by CPT median operative minutes times 60; then multiplied by specialty dollars/RVU to model compensation/hour
comparator.aggregation: Overall comparisons weighted by case volume
comparator.complexity: Technical/anatomic matching; no reported multivariable case-mix/complexity adjustment

results.outcome: modeled median USD per operative hour
results.interpretation: Specialty compensation model, not observed Medicare reimbursement

results.outcome: specialty compensation USD per RVU, historical to contemporary
results.arithmetic_caution: Authors report 14% for OBGYN; conventional baseline-relative change from 44.50 to 52.02 is about 16.9%. Preserve the raw rates and flag rather than silently endorsing the percentage.

studies.uncertainty: IQRs are distribution summaries, not confidence intervals. No confidence interval for the between-group difference is reported in the extracted results.
author_reported_limitations: Concurrent/other CPT exclusions omit routinely combined operations.
Voluntary NSQIP major-surgery sample may not generalize to all US patients.
Only half the earlier 24 pairs were available; several selected procedures are oncologic.
Global-period fees and perioperative work not accounted for.
reviewer_concerns_not_formal_risk_of_bia: Code-specific case counts range from 2 to 3184; sparse procedures have unstable time summaries and aggregate results reflect case mix.
Time normalization alone does not standardize intensity, risk, full episode work or patient complexity.
Different specialty compensation multipliers mechanically affect the modeled dollar comparison; physician sex/gender is not analyzed.
Patient gender identity and Medicare age/entitlement strata are not established.
Some published table arithmetic differs from the stated formula; exact source cells and a separate arithmetic check are retained in L-P03_table1.json.
studies.proposed_status: Retain; full-text extraction advanced in this session. Classify as service valuation with registry time data and modeled specialty compensation, not cisgender patient disparity or physician-gender outcome evidence.

synthesis.pooling: Do not pool the three headline contrasts: pair definitions, time denominators, year and compensation constructs differ.
synthesis.supported: Results vary with the selected codes and metric. L-P02 is null; L-P03 favors female-specific procedures on RVU/hour while favoring male-specific procedures on modeled specialty compensation/hour. L-P01's broader anatomical comparison reports male-higher valuation.
synthesis.not_supported: No causal attribution, access effect, national patient spending disparity, physician-gender payment effect or universal valuation pattern is established by these three studies.
next_checks: Obtain L-P01 and L-P02 peer-reviewed full texts without bypassing access controls.
Audit pair-level comparability and overlap before any quantitative synthesis.
Resolve L-P02 count discrepancy and obtain numerical confidence intervals.
Clarify L-P01 historical subset, time adjustment and exact Medicare pricing inputs.
Preserve L-P03 raw rates and verify percentage/table arithmetic before reuse.
